glosses: To suffer decomposition due to biological action, especially by fungi or bacteria.

examples.text: The apple left in the cupboard all that time had started to rot.
Fix'd like a plant on his peculiar spot, / To draw nutrition, propagate, and rot.

glosses: To decline in function or utility.

examples.text: Your brain will rot if you spend so much time on the computer, Tony!

glosses: To (cause to) deteriorate in any way, as in morals; to corrupt.
To make putrid; to cause to be wholly or partially decomposed by natural processes.

examples.text: to rot vegetable fiber

glosses: To spend a long period of time (in an unpleasant place or state).

examples.text: to rot in prison
to rot in Hell
If I hadn't rotted in bed all day I would've come...
Four of the sufferers were left to rot in irons.
Rot, poor bachelor, in your club.

glosses: To expose, as flax, to a process of maceration, etc., for the purpose of separating the fiber; to ret.
To talk nonsense.

examples.text:
“Did they hang you well?” said Porson.
“Don’t rot,” said Mr Watkins; “I don’t like it.”

Adrian thought it worth while to try out his new slang. ‘I say, you fellows, here's a rum go. Old Biffo was jolly odd this morning. He gave me a lot of pi-jaw about slacking and then invited me to tea. No rotting! He did really.’

glosses: The process of becoming rotten; putrefaction.
Decaying matter.

examples.text: When a turkey vulture detects the scent of rot, it circles down, tracing the plume of chemicals to its source.

glosses: Any of several diseases in which breakdown of tissue occurs.

examples.text: His cattle must of rot and murrain die.

glosses: Verbal nonsense.

examples.text: You're talking rot! I don't believe a word.

glosses: To rot, decay or putrefy.

examples.text: Plastics can take centuries to decompose.
